blocks.text:
I need to find chain C residues with heavy atoms within 4.0 Å of chain D atoms. Chain C spans residues 52-96 and chain D spans 21-51, forming what looks like a coiled-coil helix pair, so I'm checking the coordinate ranges of both chains to narrow down which regions are likely to be close enough to form the interface.

I'm going through the CA coordinates for each residue in chain C to map out the helix's path through space and identify which residues' positions overlap spatially with chain D's range.

Continuing to list out Chain D CA coordinates...

Looking at the spatial arrangement, I'm checking whether chains C and D run antiparallel to each other and trying to identify where their residues come close enough to form contacts, estimating CA-CA distances between specific residue ranges to see if this forms a four-helix bundle arrangement.

I'm listing out the coordinates for chains C and D residues in the overlapping y-range (roughly 60-77 for C, 40-51 for D) so I can compute pairwise distances and identify which residues form the closest contacts between the two helices.

Looking specifically at D50 (ASN) side chain atoms against nearby chain C residues, I check the distance between D50's ND2 and C69's CB — it comes out to about 3.29 Å, well within contact range, confirming ARG69 on chain C interacts with ASN50 on chain D.

Then checking D46 (VAL), I trace its CG1 atom against LEU73's side chain on chain C to see if that's another contact point.

Confirmed - that distance comes out to roughly 3.62Å, another valid contact. Given how many close contacts appear along this stretch, I realize I need a more systematic approach: since these chains are antiparallel helices, I should bin the atoms by position along the helical axis and scan chain D residues against nearby chain C residues within a reasonable window, rather than checking pairs ad hoc.

I'm listing out coordinates for chain D residues starting from residue 21 to build this systematic comparison.

Still listing coordinates...

Still listing atomic coordinates...

Listing more residue coordinates...

Still listing atomic coordinates...

Still listing residue coordinates...

Now I need to figure out which chain C residues might sit near chain D at the interface, focusing on residues around 65-96 and possibly 61-64, since chain D's x-coordinates range from about -18 to +1.5, so I'm checking which chain C atoms fall into that same range.

Still recording coordinates...

Still listing atomic coordinates...

Still listing atomic coordinates...

Still recording coordinates...

Continuing to list out coordinates for residues 88 through 91...

Still recording atom coordinates...

Now I'm checking whether chain C residues 61-69 could be spatially close to chain D's last residue (51), comparing their x/y/z positions to see if any contacts fall within a reasonable distance threshold.

I find that C69's NH1 atom is close enough to D50's O atom (~2.29Å) to count as a contact, confirming this interface point. Checking C69 against D51's N atom shows the distance is too far, so I move on to systematically mapping chain C residues 70-96 against chain D, noticing that chain C runs from high to low y-values while chain D runs low to high, suggesting an antiparallel arrangement between the two chains.

Based on this antiparallel pattern, I estimate a rough pairing formula: for chain C residue i, the corresponding chain D residue is approximately 119 minus i, give or take a few positions. I also notice an x-coordinate offset between the chains, with chain C generally sitting at larger x-values than chain D, leaving a gap that side chains must bridge to make contact, so I'll need to check each residue pair's distances individually rather than relying purely on the y-based estimate.

Checking C70 against nearby D residues, the x-gap is too large (~9Å) for any atom contact, so I'm ruling that one out. Same story for C71 — the closest D atom is still around 7.6Å away, so no contact there either.

For C72 lysine, I'm comparing its side chain atoms against D45 and D49 candidates, but the distances all come out just above the 4Å cutoff (around 4.3-4.4Å), so this residue doesn't appear to form a direct contact either.

Then checking C72 CG against D49 OE1 gives a distance around 3.75Å — that's within the contact threshold, so C:K72 does make contact. Moving to C73 leucine, CD2 comes out to about 3.62Å from D46 CG1, confirming another valid contact for C:L73. C74 methionine is ruled out since chain D's x-range doesn't overlap with chain C's residue 74 positions (8.9Å gap). Now I'm working through C75 glutamate's side chain atoms against D42 to check for any contacts there.

For C76 threonine, I'm computing distances between its side chain atoms and D42's glutamate residue — OG1 to OE2 comes out to roughly 3.97Å, which just squeaks inside the 4.0Å contact cutoff, so C:T76 counts as a contact. I'm now checking the remaining C76 atoms (CB, CG2) against D42 and D43 to see if any other pairs also qualify.

Moving to C77 leucine, I'm measuring its CD1/CD2 atoms against nearby D-chain residues like D43's isoleucine and D39's leucine, but the x-coordinate gap alone exceeds 6Å, so there's no contact here. This pattern suggests the two helices sit roughly 6-10Å apart overall, with only occasional long side chains bridging the gap to create sporadic contacts rather than a continuous interface.

Continuing down the sequence, C78 lysine's coordinates put it far from any D-chain atoms (x-difference too large), so I'm ruling that out too. Then C79 glutamate's OE1 atom comes within 3.78Å of D39's CD1, which qualifies as a genuine contact, so I'm adding C:E79 to the list.

For C80 alanine, I'm checking distances to D39's CD2 side chain atom — the CA measures 3.80Å away, confirming another contact, so C:A80 goes on the list too. Moving to C81 arginine, its atoms are all too far (7.8Å+) from the nearest D-chain residues like D36's threonine, so no contact there.

Checking C82 glutamine next, its N, CA, and CB atoms are similarly distant (7Å+) from D35's glutamate and D36's atoms, ruling out contact. Now I'm working through C83 glutamine's full atom list against D35's glutamate side chain and D36's threonine, calculating whether NE2 falls within contact range of D35's OE1 oxygen.

Distance calcs confirm both C83's contacts with D35 OE1 (~3.53Å) and D36 OG1 (~2.97Å) — adding Q83 to the contact list. Moving to C84 leucine, I check its backbone and side chain against D36's CG2 and D32's CD1, but the z-coordinate gap of roughly 8Å rules out any contact. C85 leucine's atoms also sit too far in x from the nearby D-chain residues (D32, D33) to register a contact, so I'm marking it clear and moving on to examine C86 alanine's coordinates next.

I confirm both D36 OG1 and CG contacts with C87, giving distances around 3.58 and 3.82, so both count. Checking C88 ARG against nearby D residues shows no atoms within contact range since z-values differ too much, so C88 has no contact. Moving to C89 GLU, I'm now computing its backbone and side-chain coordinates to check against the D chain.

For C90 GLU, I calculate OE2 to D28 CD comes out to about 3.96, just barely within contact range, and OE2 to D28 NE gives roughly 3.24, confirming a real contact — so I'm adding C90:D28 as a confirmed pair. I'm now checking the CD-to-NE distance for additional confirmation of this same contact region.

Moving to C91 VAL, I check its atoms against D28/D29 and find all z-gaps exceed 4.4 with additional x offsets, so no contact here.

For C92 ASP, I compare against D28's NH2 but the z-distance is too large, so no contact for this residue either.

For C93 ARG, I'm setting up coordinates for N, CA, C, O, CB, CG, CD, NE, CZ, NH1, NH2 to compare against nearby D28 atoms next.

I find C93 CD to D28 NH2 gives a distance of 3.74 Å and C93 NE to D28 NH2 gives 3.93 Å, so both confirm a contact — I'm adding R93 to the interface list.

Now I'm checking C94 LEU's coordinates against D29 ARG's side chain atoms, and CD1 to D29 CD comes out to 3.61 Å, confirming another contact — adding L94 to the list, then continuing to check CD2 against NH1.

I'm now checking whether C95 GLY and C96 GLN have any nearby chain D atoms — both turn out too far away in z or x to count as contacts, so I'm excluding them. I'm shifting to checking chain C residues 52-68 against chain D residues near y=15.7, and starting to calculate the distance between C68 and D50 ND.

Then I go back through more borderline cases like C74, C75, and C77, computing distances between their nearby atoms and chain D's closest residues (D42, D43, D46, D47), and each time finding the gaps too large — 5 to 7 angstroms — to qualify as contacts.

Continuing through C78, C81, C82, C84, C85, C88, and C89, I check each residue's closest atom against nearby chain D atoms (D36, D39, D35, D32, D28), and in every case the x, y, or z offsets add up to more than the contact threshold, so none of these residues make contact either.

Confirming C91, C92, and C95 also fail contact checks against D28/D29/D22/D21 candidates, and C70/C71 stay confirmed as non-contacts. Compiling the full list of true contacts so far — 69, 72, 73, 76, 79, 80, 83, 86, 87, 90, 93, 94 — I notice they follow a strikingly regular i, i+3/i+4 spacing, the classic signature of a helix-helix interface, which makes me wonder if I've missed a contact near 89 or 96 that would complete the pattern.

Checking whether the pattern would extend to 97 (which doesn't exist) or 66 (whose predicted partner D53/54 is beyond the chain's end at D51) confirms there's nothing more to find there. I'm re-verifying the precise distances for C69, C72, C73, C79, and C80 against their D-chain partners, recalculating each dx/dy/dz component and summed distance to confirm they fall within contact range — all check out around 3.2–3.8 Å.

Continuing this verification through C80's other atoms, C83, C86, C87, C90, C93, and C94, confirming each falls within or outside contact thresholds as expected. I also rule out other candidate residues like C71, C75, C77, C84, C88, C95, and C96 against nearby D-chain residues, finding their closest atoms too far apart (typically 5+ Å) to count as contacts, which is consistent with the alternating pattern of contacting/non-contacting positions I've been tracking.

Checking C76 against D46 more carefully, I find a real contact at 3.70 Å between its OG1 and D46's CG2 — so C76 does interact after all. I verify a few more nearby pairs (C75/D46, C70/D50, C68/D49) and confirm they're all too far to count.

Compiling the final contact list: C69 (Arg), C72 (Lys), C73 (Leu), C76 (Thr), C79 (Glu), C80 (Ala), C83 (Gln), C86 (Ala), C87 (Leu), C90 (Glu), C93 (Arg), C94 (Leu) — now I want to double-check a few of the borderline exclusions once more before finalizing.

I should also check the long charged side chains on chain D reaching toward chain C — arginines, lysines, glutamates that I hadn't fully traced. Checking D28's guanidinium group against C90 and C93 carboxylate/guanidinium atoms confirms the closest distance is around 3.96-4.8 Å, consistent with what I'd already found. Now I'm tracing D29's arginine side chain (CD, NE, CZ, NH1, NH2) against nearby chain C residues like C94 to see if any new contacts emerge.

Checking D29's NH1 against C94's delta carbons gives contacts around 3.6-3.9 Å, so that's confirmed, but the CG distance stretches out to 5.3 Å so it's not close enough. I'm ruling out D26, D31, D34, D37, and D38 since their side chain atoms land too far in x, y, or z from any chain C residue. For D35's glutamate, the OE1/OE2 carboxylate comes close to C83's NE2 at about 3.5 Å, which is already accounted for, while its distance to C86 is too far at 5.7 Å to count.

I go through the remaining D-chain residues one by one, computing distances between their side chain atoms and nearby chain C atoms: D41, D44, D45, and D48 are all too far, but D49's OE1 makes a solid 3.75 Å contact with C72's CG. D50's ND2 confirms a 3.29 Å contact with C69's CB, while its OD1 to C69's CD falls just short at 4.2 Å. D47 and D46 don't turn up anything new, but D43's CG1 lands a genuine 3.74 Å contact with C76's CG2, confirming that pairing.

I check D39's leucine deltas against C76 and C79, finding a 3.98 Å contact with C79's CB and a borderline 3.99 Å touch with C80's CA, both consistent with residues already flagged. D36's side chain confirms contacts with C87 at 3.82-3.88 Å, and D32's CD2 reaches C86's CB at 3.84 Å, while its CD1 to C87 doesn't pan out. After double-checking that C80's neighbor L84 and residue E89 truly show no contacts, I settle on the final interface list: C:R69, C:K72, C:L73, C:T76, C:E79, C:A80, C:Q83, C:A86, C:L87, C:E90, C:R93, C:L94.
